source.publication: 2025 SC1040 Individual Income Tax Instructions (SCDOR) and the 2025 SC1040 form and tax tables (IITPacket_2025)
source.section: Instructions PDF p.10 'Line o: Social Security and/or railroad retirement if taxed on your federal return'; PDF p.11 ('railroad retirement income do[es] not qualify ... not taxed by South Carolina'); SC1040 line o, packet PDF p.46; Instructions PDF pp.10-11 'Line p-1 through line p-3: Retirement deduction', qualified retirement income definition and Worksheet for taxpayer (line p-1) lines 1-5 and Worksheet for spouse (line p-2) lines 1-5; Instructions PDF p.12 'Line q: Age 65 and older deduction' and Worksheet for taxpayer (line q-1) lines 1-4 ('against any South Carolina income'); PDF p.13 Worksheet for spouse (line q-2) lines 1-4; SC1040 lines 1-6 and 15 (packet PDF pp.46-47); Instructions PDF p.5 Line 1 (federal taxable income); Instructions PDF p.16 Line 6; Tax Rate Schedule packet PDF p.51 (6% minus 642, any filing status); brackets as derived in the record (brackets.derivation)

worked: Federal AGI = spouse wages 70,000.00 + taxpayer IRA 4,000.00 + spouse private pension 1,500.00 + taxable Social Security (85% of 30,000; given) 25,500.00 = 101,000.00. Federal taxable income = 101,000.00 - standard deduction 33,100.00 (31,500.00 joint + 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 67,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored, federal figures given, not tested). SC1040 line 1 federal taxable income 67,900.00; additions lines a-e none, line 2 = 0.00; line 3 = 67,900.00. Line o: taxable Social Security 25,500.00 subtracted (exempt). Line p-1 worksheet (taxpayer, age 70): line 1 10,000.00; line 4 IRA 4,000.00; p-1 = 4,000.00. Line p-2 worksheet (spouse, age 60, under 65): line 1 3,000.00; line 4 pension 1,500.00; p-2 = 1,500.00. Line q-1 worksheet (taxpayer 70): 15,000.00 - 4,000.00 = 11,000.00, taken against any South Carolina income on the return, here the spouse's wages; the taxpayer's own income (4,000) does not limit it. Line q-2: spouse is under 65, none. Each person's own age decides their branch. Projection: taxpayer's best_of_group keeps the age 65 entry, min(15,000, any income on the return) = 15,000 (= 4,000 + 11,000); spouse sc_retirement_under_65 = 1,500. Line 4 total subtractions = o 25,500.00 + p-1 4,000.00 + p-2 1,500.00 + q-1 11,000.00 = 42,000.00. Line 5 South Carolina income subject to tax = 67,900.00 - 42,000.00 = 25,900.00. Line 6 tax = 3% x (17,840.00 - 3,560.00) + 6% x (25,900.00 - 17,840.00) = 428.40 + 483.60 = 912.00 (same as 6% x 25,900.00 - 642 = 1,554.00 - 642.00 = 912.00); the printed table (row 25,900 to 26,000, figured at the row midpoint) gives 915; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Line 12 Two Wage Earner Credit: not modelled (warning), 0.00; it would be 0 anyway, since both spouses do not have earned income. Line 14 credits 0.00; line 15 state income tax = 912.00.
accepted_approximations: The bracket starts 3,560 and 17,840 are derived from the printed tax table and the 6%-minus-642 formula; the table fixes them only to 3,559-3,566 and 17,818-17,857. Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses the table row's midpoint.

The booklet stacks the age 65 deduction on the retirement deduction (15,000 less the retirement and military deductions taken). The projection puts the 65-or-older retirement deduction and the age 65 deduction in one best_of_group, with the age 65 cap reduced by military retirement. For a person 65 or older this gives the same total as the worksheets, the larger of 15,000 and the military retirement income (Examples 1-5), whenever the person's income covers it.
